claims.text: Noble-metal salts containing Pt, Ir, or Ru reduce at approximately 300°C before the less noble metal salts.
The initially reduced noble metals establish a stable lattice.
The initially formed noble-metal lattice promotes hydrogen adsorption and dissociation.
Hydrogen atoms generated on the noble-metal lattice reduce Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe ions.
The subsequently reduced metals incorporate into the preformed noble-metal lattice to produce a single-phase solid solution.
In Pt–Ru systems, the initially formed Pt-rich fcc phase is kinetically trapped.
A Ru-rich hcp phase is thermodynamically more stable than the initially formed Pt-rich fcc phase.
Secondary heating at 400–500°C can drive transformation from Pt-rich fcc material toward Ru-rich hcp material.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation has an activation barrier of approximately 0.45 eV.
The relative amounts of Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains control the final alloy's phase makeup and morphology.
Increasing Ru content together with secondary heating will increase the Ru-hcp phase fraction.
An increased Ru-hcp phase fraction will correlate directly with enhanced methanol-oxidation performance.
The proposed HEA nanoparticles will have significantly higher MOR mass activity than commercial Pt black and a Pt-rich fcc HEA prepared only at 300°C.
The proposed HEA nanoparticles will sustain MOR current better than commercial Pt black and the 300°C Pt-rich fcc baseline.
Commercial Johnson Matthey Pt black has an MOR mass activity of 170 mA/mgPt.
Commercial Johnson Matthey Pt black has an electrochemically active surface area of 17.59 m2/gPt.
The mechanism applies to quinary through octonary alloys containing Pt, Ir, or Ru under reduction at 300°C and optional secondary heating up to 500°C.
The mechanism does not apply to systems lacking Pt, Ir, and Ru, such as NiCoCuFe.
The mechanism does not apply to Pd-containing systems because Pd has unfavorable hydrogen desorption and higher reduction barriers.
Spray drying the homogeneously mixed precursor salts produces near-spherical, compositionally uniform precursor particles.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that sequential reduction and incorporation yield a uniform single-phase structure, whereas the mediator and outcome discuss relative fcc/hcp domain fractions and overall phase makeup, implying coexistence of multiple phases.
Pd salts are included among candidate precursors in the stated initial material system, but the boundary excludes Pd-containing systems from the proposed mechanism.
